paragraphs.text: Set in a privately owned forest twenty minutes from town, Hollybrook offers week-long residential stays for children aged 11 to 15. Camp leader Lorenzo Kask spent fourteen years as a park ranger before opening the camp, and his knowledge of local wildlife shapes much of the programme. Campers sleep in canvas tents, learn to build shelters and light fires safely, and cook their own evening meal over an open flame. Families should pack a warm sleeping bag, a waterproof jacket and sturdy shoes; a full kit list is sent out after booking. To encourage children to focus on their surroundings, mobile phones are handed in on arrival and given back on the final morning. Parents who want news of their child can ring the camp office between 7 and 8 pm on any evening. A week costs £395, including all meals.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Little Makers is a day camp for younger children, aged 5 to 8, held in the main hall of the Elm Street Community Centre. Each week has a different theme, such as 'under the sea' or 'space travel', and children paint, model with clay and build large cardboard sculptures linked to that theme. Doors open at 8.30 am and the day finishes at 4 pm. Staff stay until 4.15, but after that a charge is added for every quarter of an hour, so please plan your journey accordingly. Lunch is not provided: children need a packed lunch and a refillable water bottle every day. Because several regular attendees have serious allergies, the centre is completely nut-free, and staff check lunchboxes each morning. A week costs £140, and when two or more children from the same family attend, each additional child receives 15% off.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Run by qualified instructors at Saltmere Harbour, Coastline Sailing Camp introduces children aged 9 to 13 to small-boat sailing over five consecutive days. Mornings are spent on the water in single-handed dinghies, while afternoons cover knots, weather and basic navigation in the clubhouse. Safety comes first: before a place is confirmed, every child must show that they can swim 25 metres unaided, either at the harbour pool or at a local leisure centre, which then signs a form. Life jackets and wetsuits are provided, so children only need a swimming costume, a towel and a hat. Since the harbour is some distance from town, a coach collects campers from the railway station at 8 am and brings them back at 5 pm, at no extra cost to families. Instructor Bernadette Okwu points out that sessions may move indoors if winds become too strong. The camp costs £260 per week.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Code and Create is a two-week technology camp for teenagers aged 12 to 16, based in the computer suite of Northgate Library. No previous experience is required. In the first week, participants learn the basics of a beginner-friendly programming language; in the second, they plan, design and test a simple video game of their own, working in pairs to give each other feedback. Laptops are provided, so there is no need to bring one from home. Coordinator Ayesha Thornbury explains that the aim is to show young people that technology is something they can create, not just consume. On the final Friday afternoon, parents, grandparents and friends are invited to a showcase where every participant presents and demonstrates their finished game. Places are limited to twenty, and the fee for the full fortnight is £310. Sessions run from 10 am to 3 pm.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Green Thumbs Farm Camp takes place at Mill Lane Farm, a working family farm on the edge of town, and is designed for children aged 7 to 11. Farmer Fenella Draycott and her team show campers how to feed the goats and chickens, collect eggs and look after the vegetable beds. Children plant seeds on their first day, and at the end of the week each child goes home with a basket of the salad leaves and herbs they have helped to grow. Mud is unavoidable, so campers should wear old clothes and bring wellington boots. The camp costs £175 a week, but a limited number of bursaries covering the full fee are available for families on low incomes. Applications for these must reach the farm office by 30 April, and successful families are informed in mid-May.
paragraphs.label: E

A. Set in a privately owned forest twenty minutes from town, Hollybrook offers week-long residential stays for children aged 11 to 15. To encourage children to focus on their surroundings, mobile phones are handed in on arrival and given back on the final morning. Parents who want news of their child can ring the camp office between 7 and 8 pm on any evening. A week costs £395, including all meals.

B. Little Makers is a day camp for younger children, aged 5 to 8, held in the main hall of the Elm Street Community Centre. Each week has a different theme, such as 'under the sea' or 'space travel', and children paint, model with clay and build large cardboard sculptures linked to that theme. Doors open at 8.30 am and the day finishes at 4 pm. Staff stay until 4.15, but after that a charge is added for every quarter of an hour, so please plan your journey accordingly. Lunch is not provided: children need a packed lunch and a refillable water bottle every day. Because several regular attendees have serious allergies, the centre is completely nut-free, and staff check lunchboxes each morning. A week costs £140, and when two or more children from the same family attend, each additional child receives 15% off.

C. Run by qualified instructors at Saltmere Harbour, Coastline Sailing Camp introduces children aged 9 to 13 to small-boat sailing over five consecutive days. Mornings are spent on the water in single-handed dinghies, while afternoons cover knots, weather and basic navigation in the clubhouse. Safety comes first: before a place is confirmed, every child must show that they can swim 25 metres unaided, either at the harbour pool or at a local leisure centre, which then signs a form. Life jackets and wetsuits are provided, so children only need a swimming costume, a towel and a hat. Since the harbour is some distance from town, a coach collects campers from the railway station at 8 am and brings them back at 5 pm, at no extra cost to families. Instructor Bernadette Okwu points out that sessions may move indoors if winds become too strong. The camp costs £260 per week.

D. Code and Create is a two-week technology camp for teenagers aged 12 to 16, based in the computer suite of Northgate Library. No previous experience is required. In the first week, participants learn the basics of a beginner-friendly programming language; in the second, they plan, design and test a simple video game of their own, working in pairs to give each other feedback. On the final Friday afternoon, parents, grandparents and friends are invited to a showcase where every participant presents and demonstrates their finished game. Places are limited to twenty, and the fee for the full fortnight is £310. Sessions run from 10 am to 3 pm.

E. Green Thumbs Farm Camp takes place at Mill Lane Farm, a working family farm on the edge of town, and is designed for children aged 7 to 11. Farmer Fenella Draycott and her team show campers how to feed the goats and chickens, collect eggs and look after the vegetable beds. questions.evidence: a limited number of bursaries covering the full fee are available for families on low incomes

explanation.uk: В абзаці E родинам із низьким доходом пропонують стипендії. Знижка з абзацу B залежить від кількості дітей, а не від доходу.

questions.prompt: transport provided at no charge
questions.evidence: a coach collects campers from the railway station at 8 am and brings them back at 5 pm, at no extra cost to families

explanation.en: Paragraph C describes a free coach between the railway station and the harbour. Paragraph B only tells parents to plan their own journey.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C описан бесплатный автобус между железнодорожным вокзалом и гаванью. В абзаце B родителям лишь советуют самим спланировать дорогу.
explanation.uk: В абзаці C описано безкоштовний автобус між залізничним вокзалом і гаванню. В абзаці B батькам лише радять самим спланувати дорогу.
